nodes.label: Grouping and Text Wrapping Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: grouping and text wrapping implementation plan

nodes.label: Authoring-Only Grouping
nodes.rationale: Grouping exists for authoring only: exports flatten groups so rendering never depends on the group tree.

nodes.label: Non-Destructive Ungroup
nodes.rationale: Ungroup restores child coordinates instead of deleting them, so grouping round-trips without data loss.

nodes.label: Geometry-Derived Wrap Width
nodes.rationale: Wrap width is derived from box geometry and font metrics rather than stored, so resizing a box rewraps text automatically.

nodes.label: Full-Span Divider Guides
nodes.rationale: Divider guides span the full page because they mark where the bill grows, not just the container they were created in.

nodes.label: Resize Snaps to Guides Only (Position Drag)
nodes.norm_label: resize snaps to guides only (position drag)
nodes.rationale: Resize is intentionally not snapped to guides; only position dragging snaps, because resizing against guides duplicated edge logic.

nodes.label: Snap Engine
nodes.rationale: The snap engine is the single decision point for dragging; canvas and inspector call it instead of duplicating threshold math.

nodes.label: Paper Normalization First
nodes.rationale: Paper normalization first: every billPart's pixels are mapped to the template's paper space so downstream code never handles mixed coordinate systems.

nodes.label: Recapture Two-Step Flow
nodes.rationale: Recapture is a two-step explicit flow (verify, then accept) because an automatic recapture silently overwrote table data that the user could not get back.

nodes.label: Authoring-Only Grouping
nodes.rationale: Grouping is an editor convenience only; the exported bill must stay byte-identical whether or not shapes are grouped.

nodes.label: Nested Group Cycle Guard
nodes.rationale: Groups can nest freely, so a cycle guard is required before membership can be persisted safely.

nodes.label: Downward-Growing Wrapping Text
nodes.rationale: A fixed-width text box wraps and grows downward without clipping; the grown box floats so neighbouring content is never pushed.

nodes.label: Independent Per-Axis Snapping
nodes.rationale: Each axis snaps independently, so one gesture can catch an edge horizontally and a centre vertically and emit two guides at once.

nodes.label: Full-Span Rule Divider
nodes.rationale: A rule snapped across a shape draws beyond it and becomes a divider line for the full page span.

nodes.label: Three Snap Levels per Axis
nodes.rationale: Left, centre and right plus top, centreY and bottom give Instagram-style alignment without a snap settings panel.

nodes.label: Paper Background Normalization
nodes.rationale: Scan paper tint is normalized toward white so the cutout blends into the digital bill instead of showing as a grey box.

nodes.label: Cutout Recapture
nodes.rationale: Recapture re-runs extraction from the current position so a bad crop is repaired in place instead of requiring a full redraw.

nodes.label: Two-Column Screen Layout
nodes.rationale: The screen is split into a wide primary column (placeholder text plus a large content image box) and a narrower right sidebar stack (thumbnail box over a card panel), a conventional scannable content-page pattern that separates main narrative content from supporting elements.

nodes.label: Tinted Bill (e2e invoice fixture)
nodes.rationale: Synthetic invoice fixture with a cream/tinted (non-white) background used in e2e tests to verify that document/invoice extraction handles colored backgrounds and low-contrast surfaces, not just plain white scans.

nodes.label: Tinted Cream Background
nodes.rationale: The fixture deliberately uses a beige/tinted page background (vs pure white) so e2e tests can detect regressions where extraction or rendering assumes white paper.

nodes.label: Bill Part Tool
nodes.rationale: Bill Part cuts can keep or whiten the paper's own colour; the whitening default is set in the Reference Image panel while each part keeps its own choice and can be re-cut from its Bill Part panel — parts are re-editable semantic regions of the bill.

nodes.label: Fill & Render (primary action)
nodes.rationale: Styled as the single primary (blue) button in the header, indicating the end-state of the template workflow: resolve placeholders to values and produce the rendered bill.

nodes.label: {{token}} Placeholder Binding
nodes.rationale: Placeholders type their own input (label, input type, printed style), making the template self-describing so Fill & Render can prompt for or bind data without external schema.

nodes.label: Placeholders Panel ({{token}} mechanism)
nodes.rationale: Add a {{token}} to a text box or drop in an image placeholder to make it appear in rendered output; each placeholder carries its own label, input type and printed style — tokens are the binding layer between template design and Fill & Render data.

nodes.label: Properties Panel (empty-selection state)
nodes.rationale: Copy reads 'Nothing selected. Pick an object on the canvas to edit its geometry, styling and semantic role.' — confirms selection-driven editing and that objects carry a semantic role alongside geometry and styling.

nodes.label: Template Placeholder Field System
nodes.rationale: Curly-brace {field_N} syntax indicates the layout is a reusable template whose regions are bound to data fields at render time rather than hard-coded content.

nodes.label: Wireframe Layout with Placeholder Fields
nodes.rationale: Low-fidelity wireframe uses abstract bordered boxes instead of real content so layout structure and proportions can be validated before visual design; a four-block grid (one large content area top-left, three smaller blocks) implies an asymmetric master-detail or media-plus-details screen.

nodes.label: Two-Column Asymmetric Wireframe Layout Pattern
nodes.rationale: Low-fidelity wireframe composition: dense filler-character text block simulates a paragraph of body copy in the top-left, while empty bordered rectangles on the right and bottom stand in for media and secondary content. The deliberate use of placeholder greeking and empty boxes defers visual/style decisions so the prototype can validate content hierarchy and a two-column (text-left, media-right) layout before committing to real content or styling.

nodes.label: Asymmetric Panel Grid Pattern
nodes.rationale: Low-fidelity layout sketch of a screen with a single outer frame containing two unequal columns: the left column holds a large square panel (dominant media/hero content) above a wide shorter panel, while the right column stacks a short, a medium, and a taller panel. The asymmetric panel sizes suggest a content hierarchy prioritizing one primary element with supporting secondary cards, typical of a dashboard, gallery, or product detail skeleton.

nodes.norm_label: three type roles (bitter, archivo, ibm plex mono)
nodes.rationale: Three type roles: Bitter slab serif for the wordmark and headlines, Archivo for UI text, IBM Plex Mono for anything a machine reads - variables, guide ids, coordinates, money.

nodes.label: Canvas Token Mirror
nodes.rationale: Canvas overlays cannot read CSS variables, so the token set is mirrored in components/ui/tokens.ts with a drift test keeping the two copies in sync.

nodes.label: Controls API Stability
nodes.rationale: Many files consume Controls.tsx, so the redesign restyles it under a frozen public API to avoid cascading edits across consumers.

nodes.label: Design Token Layer
nodes.rationale: Single source of truth for the redesign: colour, type and spacing tokens defined in app/globals.css so every surface of the editor draws from one palette.

nodes.label: Toast Queue
nodes.rationale: Queue logic kept pure and node-testable in lib/client/toastQueue.ts; DOM concerns are isolated behind a client provider in the root layout.

nodes.label: Four-Column Editor Shell
nodes.rationale: Tool rail, context column, stage and inspector give every region of the editor a stable home and predictable width.

nodes.label: Derived Step State
nodes.rationale: Step completion is computed from real document state rather than stored, so the guide can never drift from the document itself.

nodes.label: Editor-Owned Current Step
nodes.rationale: Auto-advance only fires when the current step own fact flips, so a manually chosen step is never yanked away while the user works.

nodes.label: Owner Vocabulary Rewrite
nodes.rationale: Engineering words such as parent, container and z-index are replaced with the owner vocabulary so features are found by intent rather than by data model.

nodes.label: Exported Bill Fidelity Constraint
nodes.rationale: The redesign stops at interface chrome: exported documents, layout maths and the template format must stay untouched so already-printed bills remain valid.

nodes.label: Five-Step Guided Path
nodes.rationale: A step guide that never gates keeps a non-technical owner oriented while experts can skip straight to any tool.

nodes.label: Ledger Stamp and Marker Visual Language
nodes.norm_label: ledger stamp and marker visual language
nodes.rationale: Colour roles carry meaning: a ledger is data, a stamp is a destructive action or error and a marker is a warning, so the interface speaks without jargon.

nodes.label: Byte-Identical Output
nodes.rationale: Same template and values always produce the same bytes, which lets golden tests detect regressions through the template hash.

nodes.label: Pure HTML Renderer
nodes.rationale: The renderer is a pure function of template and values with no Fabric, React, DOM or network dependency, so any host can render a bill.

nodes.label: Inert Self-Contained HTML
nodes.rationale: Output is one inert HTML file with no external stylesheet, web font, remote image or script, so it prints and shares anywhere.

nodes.label: Canonical JSON and SHA-256 (Task 2)
nodes.rationale: Canonical JSON and a hand-written SHA-256 make the template hash stable so goldens and packages can detect byte changes.

nodes.label: Freehand Path Data Fix (Task 1)
nodes.rationale: Freehand strokes were dropped from every export because path data was not carried into the HTML; the fix corrects serialisation instead of special-casing the renderer.

nodes.label: Pure HTML Renderer (renderHtml)
nodes.rationale: The renderer is a pure function of template and values with no Fabric, React, DOM or network dependency, so any host - web, share kit or server - can render a bill.

nodes.label: Golden Files and Purity Guard (Task 8)
nodes.rationale: A purity guard bans engine and impure imports inside lib/render and byte-for-byte goldens catch drift, so the renderer cannot silently become stateful.

nodes.label: The .btpkg Format
nodes.rationale: The .btpkg format reuses the existing zip and canonical JSON pipeline so packages are reproducible byte-for-byte and can be hashed.

nodes.label: Byte-Level Hashing, Not Structure Hashing
nodes.rationale: Hashes are computed over bytes, not parsed structures, so whitespace or serializer changes cannot hide behind identical objects.

nodes.label: Package Type Resolution
nodes.rationale: Machines without whichever format a package uses must still open every existing document; unknown sections are rejected loudly instead of ignored.

nodes.label: Canvas Image Conversion Viewport Gate
nodes.rationale: Canvas image conversion is gated by a feature flag and only runs in the viewport, because off-screen conversion cost broke larger documents.

nodes.label: Largest Remainder Rounding
nodes.rationale: Largest remainder rounding makes displayed column totals land exactly on the target width without a build step.

nodes.label: Snapshot-Based Resize
nodes.rationale: Table resizing snapshots the original cell widths on first drag so the operation is non-destructive and repeatable.

nodes.label: Reference Export-Leak Guard
nodes.rationale: Traced objects filtering keeps the reference id out of serialized and exported output so the scanned image can never leak into a bill.

nodes.label: Pan Clamp to Image Bounds
nodes.rationale: The viewport can never be panned past the image edge, so the page can never be lost off screen.

nodes.label: Proportional Table Column Resize
nodes.rationale: Side-marker resize scales all columns proportionally and idempotently, keeping table geometry faithful to the page.

nodes.label: Reference Image as Canvas Background
nodes.rationale: Making the reference the canvas background instead of a locked object removes a whole class of leaks and makes image and canvas read as one surface.

nodes.label: Wheel Zoom at Cursor
nodes.rationale: Plain wheel zooms under the cursor so navigation needs no modifier keys and the point of interest stays fixed while zooming.

nodes.label: Purity Guard in the Shared Package
nodes.norm_label: purity guard in the shared package

nodes.norm_label: re-export shims for web app imports

nodes.label: feature:templates Module
nodes.rationale: The library lives in its own feature:templates module wired with the templates route, so template browsing stands alone as a feature.

nodes.label: Wiring the Existing Ktor Client
nodes.rationale: Store downloads use the shared Ktor client instance and diesel deps already present in the app instead of adding new libraries.

nodes.label: BillKit Format Package
nodes.rationale: Rendering must be byte-identical on phone and server, so the format lives in one package consumed verbatim by both rather than duplicated.

nodes.label: No Build Step
nodes.rationale: No build step: pure functions plus html2canvas as a peer dependency keep the package installable in any host.

nodes.norm_label: render share and rendering polish spec

nodes.label: Form Input Name Keys
nodes.rationale: Generated inputs carry name keys matching placeholder keys so browser autofill and end-to-end selectors keep working across app and share kit.

nodes.label: Slot-Owned Style Binding
nodes.rationale: Style is applied when filling slots in fillTemplate rather than while rendering, keeping the renderer pure and letting each slot own its styling.

nodes.label: DOCX Export as Flow Approximation
nodes.rationale: DOCX export is deliberately a flow approximation - Word reflows text, so page geometry cannot be preserved; the HTML document is the fidelity export.

nodes.label: Manual Tracing (No OCR)
nodes.rationale: Manual tracing instead of OCR: the user draws boxes over the reference photo and marks them as data. Nothing is uploaded - the scan stays in the browser via FileReader, which keeps shop documents private and the output faithful.

nodes.label: Page and Reference Image as One Surface
nodes.norm_label: page and reference image as one surface
nodes.rationale: The page and the reference image are one bound surface: zooming and panning move both together so traced geometry stays aligned with the scan.

nodes.norm_label: billkit variable layout - hierarchical containers, expandable fields, two-axis guides (new_expandable)

nodes.label: Six-Stage Render Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Rendering is described as six stages from template acquisition to printing; printing (HTML to PDF) is the only impure step, everything before it stays deterministic.

nodes.label: Acquisition and Refusal (TemplateParser.kt)
nodes.rationale: TemplateParser refuses templates it cannot fully understand instead of guessing, so an unknown template can never produce a silently wrong bill.

nodes.label: Values, Not Formulas
nodes.rationale: The paper must match the data the shop already recorded - never re-derive it. Totals are stored values, not formulas recalculated at print time.

nodes.label: Version-Pinned Reprint Path
nodes.rationale: A reprint resolves the original template version stored on the document, so an old bill reprints identically even after its template changes.

nodes.label: Whitelisted Expression Calculator (Expressions.kt)
nodes.rationale: Expressions run through a whitelisted calculator so template arithmetic is possible without executing arbitrary code.

nodes.label: Pure Calculation Separated from Browser Measurement
nodes.norm_label: pure calculation separated from browser measurement
nodes.rationale: Keep pure calculations separate from browser measurement: the solver decides geometry deterministically, the browser only reports intrinsic content size.

nodes.label: Guide Movement Demands and Propagation
nodes.rationale: Objects propagate growth to guides as movement demands that are applied and re-measured until convergence, so one field growing can shift a whole structural line.

nodes.label: Eight Phases with Gates and Mandatory Reconnaissance
nodes.norm_label: eight phases with gates and mandatory reconnaissance
nodes.rationale: Eight phases with mandatory repository reconnaissance first - changing a live layout engine without auditing what already works risks silent regressions.

nodes.label: Coding-Agent Guardrails (Section 16)
nodes.rationale: Do not mutate base geometry during rendering and do not infer parent membership or guide attachments - inference at render time would corrupt the stored template.

nodes.label: Hierarchical Container Expansion
nodes.rationale: Containers resolve inner to outer so a nested rectangle's growth propagates outward predictably.

nodes.label: Two-Axis Marking Guides
nodes.rationale: Both guide orientations must work in the first complete implementation: real bills need horizontal and vertical structural lines, so X-axis expansion cannot ship as a stub.

nodes.label: Additive Completion Guarantee
nodes.rationale: Completion work is purely additive: existing tests and goldens may not change, so regressions surface immediately.

nodes.label: Container Padding Limits in the Solver
nodes.norm_label: container padding limits in the solver
nodes.rationale: Container padding limits are enforced in the solver, because padding the user sees must match the padding the solver assumes.

nodes.label: Dead Validations Removed
nodes.rationale: Dead validations were removed rather than forced to pass: the completion plan deletes checks that no longer correspond to any invariant.

nodes.label: X-Axis Expansion Evidence
nodes.rationale: X-axis expansion needs evidence on real bills - the plan traces X-axis behavior through the solver and pins it with new tests.

nodes.label: carryTo Root Cause
nodes.rationale: carryTo propagated movement to boxes that had not crossed the guide, making bottom rows jump onto it; the fix restricts how movement is carried.

nodes.label: Guide Attachment Disabled Containment
nodes.rationale: A guide attachment disabled containment - the parent frame only grew when the field nearly arrived; attachment and containment must stay independent.

nodes.label: Idempotent Layout Fixpoint
nodes.rationale: The fix must keep the idempotency property: running the solver twice must move nothing the second time.

nodes.rationale: Skeleton invoice showing company header 'ACME TRADING CO / INVOICE', PO No and invoice date meta blocks, BILL TO block, a description/qty/price table with items and Subtotal/Total rows, and a footer note — the intended trace target for a complete bill template.

nodes.label: Bill Template Maker UI
nodes.rationale: Screenshot shows a single-page bill/invoice template editor: a top action bar (Bill Template Maker brand, Open Bill, Save Template, Save to My Templates, primary Fill & Render button, Share as .html, Load Template, Undo/Redo, Preview, Export), a horizontal tool palette, left panels (Reference Image, Grid, Document, Placeholders), a central dotted design canvas tracing a reference invoice, and right panels (Properties, Layers) above a zoom/status bar. Purpose: design bill templates by tracing a reference image, place semantic parts/fields/placeholders, then fill with data and export.

nodes.label: Design Canvas (794 x 1123 bill sheet)
nodes.rationale: A4-proportioned page (794 x 1123 px, matching status bar) on a 10px visible grid at 50% zoom; the status bar reports Objects: 0 / Selected: 0, indicating the reference image has not yet been traced into editable objects.

nodes.label: Data field placeholder {{customer_name}}
nodes.rationale: Fields use a mustache-style {{...}} placeholder rendered on the canvas and listed in the Data fields panel (Customer Name), giving named, reusable slots that Fill & print can substitute per bill.

nodes.label: Designer canvas with bill template
nodes.rationale: The traced bill (ACME Trading Co invoice, page 794x1123 at 50% zoom) stays visible under a dotted grid while marking, so fields are placed directly over the printed layout they replace.

nodes.label: Field tool
nodes.rationale: Dedicated Field tool (keyboard shortcut F) keeps data-marking a distinct authoring mode from drawing, so variable regions are explicit objects rather than plain text.

nodes.label: Five-step template authoring workflow
nodes.rationale: The stepper (Your bill, Trace, Mark data, Test, Save & share) sequences template creation so each step has one job: capture the source bill, overlay its structure, tag variable data, verify with sample data, then export.

nodes.label: Mark data step (step 3)
nodes.rationale: Mark what changes each time: fields, variables, repeating rows. Separating marking from drawing lets one traced template serve any bill instance by substituting data at fill time.

nodes.label: Mark data step screenshot (Bill Template Maker)
nodes.norm_label: mark data step screenshot (bill template maker)

nodes.label: ACME Trading Co Invoice (INV-1001) - test-bill.png
nodes.rationale: Synthetic black-and-white invoice fixture used by e2e tests for document/bill parsing. Deliberately simple layout: a bordered header band, a two-cell metadata row (invoice no/date | bill-to), a plain table of two line items, and a footer note. Notable quirks: the vendor title 'ACME TRADING CO' overlaps the 'INVOICE' header text, and the Subtotal/Total labels render with no values - properties that exercise layout/OCR robustness and guard against hallucinated amounts in extraction tests.

nodes.label: Content-Addressed Storage
nodes.rationale: Stored filenames are content hashes, so uploading the same file twice cannot fork the library.

nodes.label: Deterministic Zip Output
nodes.rationale: Zip bytes must be identical across machines, so entries use fixed timestamps and sorted names; tests compare identical bytes.

nodes.label: Single Small Express Service
nodes.rationale: A single small Express service with a pocketbase-style catalog API keeps the first deployment to one process and one volume.

nodes.label: Validation Delegation to the Client
nodes.rationale: The server validates uploads only if doing so is trivial - validation is defined on the client, and the server must not fork the validation rules.

nodes.label: Package Asset Directory
nodes.rationale: Separating images from the template JSON keeps base64 bloat out of the template and gives the package a place for its own assets.

nodes.label: Repeatable Line-Item Rows
nodes.rationale: Fixed-row tables silently drop extra items, so a repeating row band is needed before bills with variable item counts can render correctly.

nodes.label: Android Network and Storage Layer
nodes.rationale: The device has no HTTP client, no INTERNET permission and no local store, so a network layer must land before a template catalog can exist.
